verdict.rationale: Crossplane's own documentation says it exposes declarative APIs that "humans, automation, and AI systems can safely act on". It also says it encapsulates policies, permissions and guardrails behind a custom API layer, extending Kubernetes RBAC to every managed resource. Together these give an agent a narrow, least-privilege interface. However, nothing documents an agent-facing plan/preview step or an approval gate that blocks unapproved changes: the CLI's render and test only covers Composition Functions offline, and the helm dry-run applies to installing Crossplane itself. Missing for 10: plan/diff preview of infrastructure changes before apply, documented review/approval gates, any agent-specific credential-scoping guidance, independent or hands-on corroboration.
